manualChecks.check: Attribute the integration-lane failures — are they caused by identity-coop Phase 1?

(a) Pristine HEAD worktree, no working-tree changes at all. (c) The shared worktree containing both sessions' work.
manualChecks.result: NOT CAUSED BY THIS PHASE — PROVEN. Decisive run: the FULL integration lane in the clean worktree carrying only this phase's changes, pointed at a DEDICATED disposable database and a dedicated Redis slot, returned **528 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors** — exactly the 518 baseline plus this phase's 10 new tests. Supporting bisection: (a) pristine HEAD: 15/15 pass. (b) HEAD + only identity-coop: 15/15 pass. (c) shared worktree: 3 failed + 5 errors. The failures therefore require the concurrent session's changes to appear. Corroborating evidence: the failing test names are unstable across runs (test_stats_new_fields vs test_monthly_plan_limit_reached; errors surface as '401 User not found' and sqlalchemy IntegrityError), which matches the conftest DB/Redis isolation gap already tracked in backlog/post-docker-gate-followups_NOTE_24-07-26.md ('5 unrelated integration failures + conftest Redis-isolation hardening'). A repeat full-lane run in the isolated worktree produced a THIRD, larger, different failure set (1 failed + 18 errors) purely from shared-database contention — two worktrees plus the concurrent agent all pointing at the same retarget_agent_test DB on port 5433 — which independently confirms these failures track environment, not code.

evlConcerns.finding: Diff-guard gate definition is ambiguous. The contract says git diff --stat ... <= 12 lines but --stat emits three different numbers: 11 insertions, 5 deletions, 16 histogram-total. 11 <= 12 PASSES; 16 > 12 would FAIL. The plan own worked example (line 805) counts 6 touched lines, a fourth reading. The gate PASSES under the insertion and net-line readings and the diff matches the enumerated authorized edit set exactly, so the collision-minimization INTENT is satisfied — but the gate as written is not mechanically decidable. Recommend pinning the counting rule (suggest: insertions only) at UPDATE PROCESS.

Coverage of the hook short-circuit is real but comes from F14 and the integration legs instead. Not a gate failure; the DB-truth half was independently confirmed by the Hybrid gates in this run.
